description: Search synonyms, abbreviations, Latin variants, lay phrases and common misspellings for anatomy clinical correlations.

portal triad: portal vein, hepatic artery, bile duct

critical_term_rules.roman_numeral_rule: Roman numerals and cranial nerve labels must match exactly after normalization; do not fuzzy-match CN III to CN IV or CN VI.

direct_synonyms: which artery passes along stomach greater curvature
negative_traps: Do not answer right gastric or left gastric artery; those follow the lesser curvature.
Short gastric arteries supply mainly the fundus near the superior part of the greater curvature, not the full inferior greater-curvature arcade.
Do not confuse with gastro-omental arteries, which follow the greater curvature.
Short gastric arteries are not the main answer for the entire greater curvature arcade.
Anterior duodenal ulcers are more likely to perforate; posterior ulcers are classically associated with gastroduodenal artery bleeding.
This is the third part of the duodenum, not the first part.
Pancreatic tail lesions are more related to the splenic hilum; pancreatic head lesions classically affect the bile duct.
Tail is near spleen; head is embraced by duodenum.
The appendicular artery is from the SMA territory via ileocolic artery, not IMA.
Anatomical variations are common; do not assume the exact branching pattern without inspection in surgery.

direct_synonyms: portal vein, hepatic artery, bile duct
portal vein hepatic artery bile duct
negative_traps: Hepatic veins are not part of the portal triad; they drain directly into the IVC.

canonical_terms: inferior border of rib / costal groove
negative_traps: Do not place instruments just under a rib; that is where the main intercostal bundle runs.

canonical_terms: phrenic nerve anterior, vagus nerve posterior
negative_traps: Phrenic nerve is anterior to the root; vagus nerve is posterior.
Do not confuse with posterior interventricular artery in the posterior interventricular sulcus.
Coronary dominance depends on origin of posterior interventricular artery.
The LAD runs anteriorly; the circumflex turns around the left AV groove.
Foramen ovale transmits V3; foramen rotundum transmits V2.

canonical_terms: ICA and cranial nerves III, IV, V1, V2, VI
negative_traps: Mandibular nerve V3 is not in the cavernous sinus lateral wall.

canonical_terms: facial nerve, retromandibular vein and external carotid artery
negative_traps: Facial nerve passes through the gland but does not innervate the gland secretomotorly.
The hypoglossal nerve is motor to tongue muscles; the lingual nerve provides general sensation to anterior tongue.

canonical_terms: common/internal carotid artery, internal jugular vein and vagus nerve
negative_traps: The sympathetic trunk is not inside the carotid sheath.
Superior orbital fissure transmits CN III, IV, V1 and VI; optic canal transmits CN II.

canonical_terms: CN III, IV, V1, VI and superior ophthalmic vein
negative_traps: Optic nerve passes through optic canal, not superior orbital fissure.

canonical_terms: axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery
negative_traps: Radial nerve is classically related to the radial groove/shaft, not surgical neck.

canonical_terms: radial nerve and profunda brachii artery
negative_traps: Do not confuse with axillary nerve at surgical neck.
Median nerve is in cubital fossa anteriorly; ulnar nerve passes behind medial epicondyle.
Ulnar nerve and artery pass superficial/medial through Guyon canal region, not inside the carpal tunnel.

canonical_terms: biceps tendon, brachial artery and median nerve
negative_traps: Ulnar nerve is not a main anterior cubital fossa content; it passes posterior to medial epicondyle.

canonical_terms: femoral nerve, artery, vein and lymphatics
negative_traps: Femoral nerve is outside the femoral sheath; artery, vein and canal are within the sheath.

canonical_terms: femoral artery, femoral vein, saphenous nerve and nerve to vastus medialis
negative_traps: Femoral nerve is not an adductor canal content.
Tibial nerve runs in posterior compartment/popliteal fossa, not around fibular neck.

canonical_terms: tibial nerve, popliteal vein and popliteal artery
negative_traps: The artery is deepest, directly related to the femur/knee capsule.

canonical_terms: tibialis posterior, flexor digitorum longus, posterior tibial vessels, tibial nerve and flexor hallucis longus
direct_synonyms: Tom Dick And Very Nervous Harry
negative_traps: Anterior tibial artery is on the anterior leg/dorsum as dorsalis pedis, not in tarsal tunnel.

canonical_terms: medial circumflex femoral artery / retinacular arteries
negative_traps: The artery to the head of femur is important in children but usually not the main adult supply.
The uterine artery crosses over the ureter, not under it.
Femoral nerve passes under the inguinal ligament, not through obturator canal.

canonical_terms: pudendal nerve and internal pudendal vessels
negative_traps: They do not stay in the gluteal region; they re-enter through the lesser sciatic foramen to reach the perineum.

canonical_terms: ptosis, diplopia and possible dilated pupil
negative_traps: CN VI lesion mainly prevents abduction; CN III is broader and may involve pupil.
Superior oblique is CN IV; lateral rectus is CN VI.

canonical_terms: tongue deviation toward the side of a lower motor neuron lesion
negative_traps: Palatoglossus is supplied by vagus nerve via pharyngeal plexus.
Optic tract lesions cause contralateral homonymous hemianopia, not bitemporal hemianopia.
